ai-at-work.excerpt: The limited test covers select products and users, with a broader rollout planned for later in October.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Google is testing shopping capabilities directly through Gemini, its AI assistant, letting Indian users purchase from Flipkart without leaving the chat interface. This matters because it shows how AI assistants are becoming transaction engines, not just information tools, which means workplace communication platforms will soon need similar commerce integration to stay relevant. The real question is whether employees actually want to buy stuff through their work chat apps, or if this is just another feature nobody asked for that'll live quietly in a settings menu.

tools-tech.title: Microsoft’s new Copilot app puts everything in one place – but the price is ‘evolving’
tools-tech.excerpt: Microsoft says Copilot has gotten ‘actually really good.’ The new app has AI agents and can write code. So how much is all this going to cost?
tools-tech.dwp_take: Microsoft bundled its AI features into a single Copilot app, making it easier for users to access code generation and AI agents without jumping between tools. For digital workplace leaders, this matters because consolidation usually means lower friction adoption rates and clearer ROI conversations, but Microsoft's vague "evolving" pricing language is a classic setup for sticker shock down the line. After three decades watching Microsoft pricing, I can tell you that "we'll figure out costs later" is corporate speak for "we're still arguing internally about what to charge."

tools-tech.title: Adobe’s next platform for Creative Cloud? Your AI assistant
tools-tech.excerpt: Adobe is preparing for a future where users increasingly interact with its software through AI assistants, rather than always going directly to its applications. That’s the idea behind its expanded in
tools-tech.dwp_take: Adobe is betting that the future of Creative Cloud isn't about mastering tools but talking to AI assistants that master the tools for you, with expanded Claude integration and new Gemini connectors leading the charge. For digital workplace pros, this means your creative teams will soon be conversing with AI instead of wrestling with menus, which changes training, support, and workflow architecture overnight. Honestly, this is either going to be the smoothest productivity jump we've seen in years or the most expensive way to get your AI assistant to argue with you about kerning.

tools-tech.title: Google is set to launch a small AI data center into space
tools-tech.excerpt: On October 1, Google’s first test satellite for Project Suncatcher is set to be launched. This is the next step in the company’s plan to build AI data centers in Earth’s orbit, according to The New Yo
tools-tech.dwp_take: Google is launching a test satellite next month as part of a project to build AI data centers in orbit, aiming to tap solar energy in space instead of expanding earthbound infrastructure. This matters because if orbital computing becomes viable, it could reshape how organizations think about infrastructure costs and energy efficiency, potentially freeing up real estate and reducing carbon footprints. That said, I'll believe it when I see it actually work at scale, because "revolutionary space tech" has a way of staying revolutionary in press releases while earthbound IT teams keep buying the same old servers from the same old vendors.

tools-tech.title: Meta floats project to lay first petabit submarine fiberoptic cable

tools-tech.dwp_take: Meta is building a massive underwater fiber optic cable called Petal that will connect the US and France with more than double the capacity of today's fastest transatlantic cables. This matters because digital workplace professionals depend on reliable international connectivity, and these infrastructure plays directly affect video conferencing quality, cloud performance, and whether your London office can actually talk to your New York one without buffering. Here's the thing though: tech companies building their own cables while traditional telecom sits on aging infrastructure is basically admitting the old guard can't keep up, which tells you everything about where real investment is flowing these days.

digital-culture.dwp_take: Brian Herriot published a book called "Time Freedom" that argues you don't have to choose between career success and having an actual life, offering five practical insights for achieving better work-life balance. For digital workplace pros, this matters because we're the ones actually implementing the flexible work policies and collaboration tools that make time freedom possible, so understanding what employees actually want helps us build better solutions. Here's the thing though: most of these "time freedom" concepts have been around forever, we just keep repackaging them in new books and pretending we invented something revolutionary.

Digital workplace pros need to stay current on these shifts because the tools and strategies we implement today are only relevant if they're built on solid thinking about how work actually happens now. Honestly, if you're not reading at least a couple of these, you're probably still trying to solve 2024 problems with 2015 playbooks, which is basically professional quicksand.

digital-culture.title: Entry-level tech jobs in NYC are being cut in half by the AI boom
digital-culture.excerpt: At first glance, the tech scene in New York City appears to be thriving: OpenAI and Anthropic have been putting down roots in the city, while stalwarts of the tech industry like Google now have more t
digital-culture.dwp_take: New York City is losing entry-level tech jobs despite explosive overall growth in the sector, with companies replacing junior positions with AI tools instead of hiring people to do that work. This matters because digital workplace leaders are suddenly managing teams with fewer rungs on the career ladder, which means less mentorship happening and fewer people developing the skills they'll need in five years. We're basically watching companies optimize themselves into a talent shortage, and frankly, whoever figures out how to actually train the next generation while the market does this will own the competitive advantage.

digital-culture.title: Appeals Court Lets the Pentagon Designate Anthropic a Supply-Chain Risk
digital-culture.excerpt: The AI lab had argued multiple violations of its rights, but a divided panel of judges sided with the Trump administration.
digital-culture.dwp_take: The Pentagon successfully argued in appeals court that it can classify Anthropic as a supply-chain risk without violating the AI company's rights. This matters to digital workplace pros because it sets precedent for how government can restrict access to AI tools and vendors in secure environments, potentially affecting enterprise adoption and compliance requirements. Look, if the Pentagon doesn't trust an AI vendor, your security team probably shouldn't either, and you'll be explaining that decision to frustrated employees who can't use their preferred tools.

industry-news.title: OpenAI’s Mental Health AI Test Reveals Gaps in Context and Urgency
industry-news.excerpt: OpenAI's MentalHealthBench tests responses to 1,215 synthetic mental health conversations, revealing gaps in how AI models seek context and gauge urgency. The post OpenAI’s Mental Health AI Test Revea
industry-news.dwp_take: OpenAI's new mental health benchmark tested AI responses across over 1,200 synthetic conversations and found the models struggle to ask clarifying questions or properly assess how urgent a situation actually is. This matters because plenty of organizations are already experimenting with AI chatbots for employee wellness and mental health support, and finding out your system can't tell the difference between someone having a rough Monday and someone in real crisis is a pretty big problem. Turns out that deploying AI to handle sensitive human stuff requires more than a good language model and some optimistic thinking, which I suppose shouldn't surprise anyone who's been paying attention.
